In 1802, William Wordsworth was about to marry Mary Hutchinson.

lines.text: His sister Dorothy kept a journal at their cottage in Grasmere.
The night before the wedding, she wore his ring all night.
The next morning, she wrote in her journal.
I gave him the wedding ring, with how deep a blessing.
In the manuscript, someone scored those lines through.
Dorothy did not go to the church.
She waited in bed until her friend Sara said, they are coming.
The journal stops about three months after the wedding.

post.caption: Wordsworth's sister wore his wedding ring. In 1802, William Wordsworth was about to marry Mary Hutchinson. His sister Dorothy kept a journal at their cottage in Grasmere. The night before the wedding, she wore his ring all night. The next morning, she wrote in her journal. I gave him the wedding ring, with how deep a blessing. In the manuscript, someone scored those lines through. Dorothy did not go to the church. She waited in bed until her friend Sara said, they are coming. The journal stops about three months after the wedding.
